meta.title: Oh-a-Chord: press any key, play a chord
meta.description: An experimental chord generating app for iPad and iPhone. Press any key, play a chord, and break out of your songwriting rut. Out now.

hero.h1: Press any key. Play a chord.
hero.positioning: Oh-a-Chord is an experimental chord generating app for iPad and iPhone. It helps you break out of your songwriting rut and find interesting new chords.

promise.heading: Why this exists
promise.body: Sometimes the biggest barrier to creativity is your own muscle memory. As a musician, I hit a friction point in my songwriting: whenever I sat down at a keyboard or grabbed my guitar, my hands instinctively fell into the exact same familiar shapes. I wanted to short-circuit those habits and discover voicings I’d never naturally stumble onto.

features.label: One key, a full chord
features.what: A single octave sets the root. Chord Type buttons choose Dim, Min, Maj, Aug, Sus2 or Sus4. Modifiers (2, 6, ♭7, maj7, 9, 11) stack colour on top for as long as a finger holds them down.
features.mediaAlt: Oh-a-Chord with MAJ selected and the MAJ7 and 9 modifiers held under two fingers. The readout says Oh-a-Fmaj9 and the chord's notes are lit on the keyboard.
features.mediaCaption: MAJ plus MAJ7 and 9 held: one F key becomes Fmaj9.

features.label: Key Mode
features.what: Arm Key Mode and the next key you press becomes the root. Select MIN first for a minor key. Every press after that stays inside that key. Reach outside it and Oh-a-Chord plays a borrowed chord that still belongs, like the ♭VI or ♭VII in a major key. It never goes silent.
features.why: It's music theory you can feel rather than study. Build a progression that works before you know why it works.
features.mediaAlt: Oh-a-Chord the moment Key Mode sets the key. KEY was armed, and the finger pressing E makes E the key: the KEY button is lit blue and reads KEY: E, dots mark the E major scale including the black keys, and the E major chord sounds.
features.mediaCaption: KEY armed, then E pressed. That press sets the key; the dots mark E major.

features.label: Strum, Harp, Arp
features.what: Three independent toggles turn a held chord into a part: Strum staggers the notes like a pick across strings, Harp sweeps one or two octaves, Arp cycles up or up-and-down at the tempo you set. Latch holds the chord hands-free.
features.why: A held chord doesn't have to sit there. These are the same moves a hardware arpeggiator gives you. The notes underneath never retrigger.
features.mediaAlt: Four performance modes side by side: Strum spreads the chord low to high, Harp 2 sweeps two octaves, and Arp Up and Arp Up/Dn loop while held. Arp Up/Dn and Latch are lit.
features.mediaCaption: Arp Up/Dn with Latch on. The chord keeps cycling, hands-free.

features.label: A full synth underneath
features.what: Behind the gear icon sits the same 6-voice DSP core that powers Oh a Synth: oscillator, filter, envelopes, chorus. Every parameter is live and touchable. The keyboard stays where it is.
features.why: The one-key chord is the front door, not the whole house. Shape the sound as deep as Oh a Synth goes.
features.mediaAlt: The Filter, Reso, Attack and Release faders highlighted, with the Filter fader opening on a held Cmaj7 and the Warm Pad preset loaded.
features.mediaCaption: Filter opening on a held chord. Every fader is live.

features.label: Save your own sounds
features.what: Tweak anything in the synth editor and a save icon appears. Tap it and name the sound. It joins the preset list next to the factory bank, stored on the device.
features.why: A good sound found by accident shouldn't be lost the next time you touch a slider.
features.mediaAlt: The preset selector highlighted, set to Brass 1, above the chord panel and keyboard.
features.mediaCaption: The preset selector. Saved sounds join the list next to the factory bank.

download.heading: Get it
download.body: Oh-a-Chord is on the App Store now. It runs on iPad and iPhone in landscape, iPadOS or iOS 16 or later.

rows.label: Keyboard
rows.value: Single octave; any key plays a full chord

rows.label: Chord Type
rows.value: Dim, Min, Maj, Aug, Sus2, Sus4

rows.label: Modifiers
rows.value: 2, 6, ♭7, maj7, 9, 11. Momentary, held while a finger is down. Combine by holding several

rows.label: Key Mode
rows.value: Major or natural minor. Locks every press to a chosen key; off-scale keys play a borrowed chord, such as ♭VI or ♭VII in a major key, rather than going silent

rows.label: Performance
rows.value: Strum, Harp (1 or 2 octave sweep) and Arp (up, up/down). Each is an independent toggle. Latch holds a chord hands-free

rows.label: Voicing
rows.value: Two sliders move a held chord through the register live, with no retriggering

rows.label: Synth engine
rows.value: The same 6-voice DSP core as Oh a Synth: DCO, 24 dB/oct filter, one ADSR, BBD-style chorus. Full parameter editor behind the settings gear

rows.label: Presets
rows.value: 9 factory sounds plus unlimited saved presets of your own, stored on the device

rows.label: Platform
rows.value: iPad and iPhone, landscape only, iPadOS or iOS 16 or later

rows.label: Privacy
rows.value: No accounts, no analytics, no network requests of any kind. Saved presets never leave the device

items.q: Do I need to know music theory to use this?
items.a: No. That's the whole point. Press a key, hear a chord. Key Mode is there if you want to explore a key without knowing why a particular note works. It isn't required to get started.
Not yet. MIDI output is planned but not in this release. Oh-a-Chord is fully playable and self-contained today, with no setup.

items.q: Can I save my own sounds?
items.a: Yes. Open the settings gear and change anything in the synth editor. A save icon appears. Name it and it joins the preset list alongside the factory bank.

items.q: Does it need an internet connection?
items.a: No. Nothing about Oh-a-Chord leaves the device. No accounts, no analytics, no sync. Saved presets are a file on your device and nowhere else.

items.q: Which devices does it run on?
items.a: Any iPad or iPhone on iPadOS or iOS 16 or later. It runs in landscape. Chord controls sit under your left hand, keyboard under your right. On iPhone, Chord Type and Modifiers share one panel with a toggle, and pitch bend is left out to fit the screen.
